examples.label: Test whether a specific binary is allowed by AppLocker

notes:
=== SECURITY PROTECTIONS ENUMERATION ===
Check AV and AppLocker before deciding which tools to use and how to deliver payloads.

AV/DEFENDER CHECK:
Get-MpComputerStatus | Select AntivirusEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled,BehaviorMonitorEnabled
sc query windefend
tasklist | findstr -i defender

APPLOCKER CHECK:
Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective | select -ExpandProperty RuleCollections
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\SrpV2"

LSASS PROTECTION:
reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v RunAsPPL
0 = unprotected (dump with ProcDump/Task Manager)
1 = PPL protected (requires signed driver bypass like PPLKiller)

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
AppLocker blocking .exe → fall back to LOLBAS (certutil, rundll32, msiexec)
AppLocker blocking scripts → use InstallUtil, regsvr32, or msbuild for CLR execution
Defender enabled → use obfuscated PS, in-memory execution (IEX), or freshly compiled tools
PPL on LSASS → cannot dump with ProcDump — use Task Manager GUI or driver bypass

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
Real-time protection disabled = aggressive tool deployment safe
AppLocker not configured = no execution restrictions
PSLogging/ScriptBlock enabled = your commands are captured in event logs
Audit process creation enabled = 4688 events with command lines logged

recommended.note: Pick tooling that fits the protection posture.

name: WinPE - Enumerate Defender and AppLocker
description: Checks endpoint protections before dropping tools: Defender real-time status and effective AppLocker policy. Test whether a specific binary path is allowed for a user.

defense.why_it_works: Before running tools or exploits, enumerating active Windows defenses (Defender, AppLocker) prevents detection and avoids wasted effort. Get-MpComputerStatus reveals Defender state, while Get-AppLockerPolicy reveals execution restrictions that determine which paths and binaries are allowed.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access. PowerShell available. Rights to query WMI/AppLocker policy (standard user can query effective policy).
defense.impact: Identifies defensive gaps: if Defender real-time protection is disabled, tools can run undetected. If AppLocker is missing or misconfigured, tool execution from staging directories is unrestricted.
defense.detection: Get-MpComputerStatus and Get-AppLockerPolicy queries logged in PowerShell transcript logs. Reconnaissance pattern: standard user enumerating security configuration. SIEM: alert on security configuration query by non-admin.
defense.artifacts: PowerShell transcript: Get-MpComputerStatus and Get-AppLockerPolicy commands | Process log: PowerShell querying security config
defense.prevention: Enable PowerShell Script Block Logging and Transcript Logging. Ensure Defender and AppLocker are configured and enforced. Monitor security configuration queries in SIEM.
defense.misconfiguration: No PowerShell logging. Defender disabled or with outdated signatures. AppLocker not configured. No SIEM alerting on security configuration reconnaissance.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Attacker checks defenses:
Get-MpComputerStatus | select RealTimeProtectionEnabled, AntivirusEnabled
# RealTimeProtectionEnabled: False <- no AV scanning

Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective | select -ExpandProperty RuleCollections
# No rules returned <- no AppLocker
defense.secure_config:
# Enable Defender real-time protection
Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $false

# Configure AppLocker via GPO
# Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Application Control Policies

# Enable PowerShell logging
# HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging
# EnableScriptBlockLogging = 1
